questions.answerText: Peptide YY is located in enteroendocrine cells of the ileum and mediates slowed transit through the ileocecal region
questions.solution: Correct Option B: Peptide YY is located in enteroendocrine cells of the ileum and mediates slowed transit through the ileocecal region. Surgical resection is the most common cause of short bowel syndrome, which occurs when there is less than 200 cm of small intestine. Intestinal ischemia is the most common cause of short bowel syndrome in adults. Patients who are unable to absorb an adequate amount of nutrients will need supplementation with parenteral nutrition. The site of resection, length of remaining small bowel and colon, and presence of the ileocecal segment all impact prognosis. The remaining healthy intestine can adapt to absorb nutrients more efficiently by an increase in absorptive surface area, which occurs with growth in diameter and height of intestinal villi. The ileocecal region slows transit through the small intestine to increase absorptive capacity. Peptide YY, secreted by the enteroendocrine cells of the colon and ileum, is the primary mediator of this action, known as the ileocecal brake. Incorrect Options: Option A - Dietary fat should be restricted for most patients with short bowel syndrome: Dietary fat restriction is usually unnecessary. It is not helpful for reduction of stool volume, and restriction of fats may reduce energy intake. Option C - Glucagon-like peptide 2 is secreted by endocrine cells in the jejunum and stimulates hyperplasia of the remnant bowel: Glucagon-like peptide 2 is secreted by endocrine cells in the colon and ileum to stimulate hyperplasia of the remaining bowel after resection of the jejunum. The length of remaining small bowel necessary for successful adaptation is usually >60 cm with intact colon or >100 cm if the colon is not intact. Option D - Since most patients will require parenteral nutrition after significant resection of the small bowel, intestinal feeding should be delayed for 7-10 days after surgery: Intestinal feeding should begin as soon as possible after surgery to stimulate intestinal adaptation. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.solution: Correct Option C: Senescence Cellular senescence describes the process in which normal diploid cells lose their ability to divide. questions.solution: Correct Option D; Surgical resection This presentation suggests intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN) of the pancreas, a grossly visible neoplasm that is potentially malignant and composed of mucin-producing cells, as evidenced by the patient’s CEA (>800). questions.stem: Which of the following parasitic infections is usually associated with occult blood in stool?
questions.stemHtml: Which of the following parasitic infections is usually associated with occult blood in stool?
questions.solution: Correct Option D: Strongyloides Occult blood in stool is associated with hookworm or Strongyloides infection. Strongyloides stercoralis enters the human host when skin contacts the larvae through infected soil usually contaminated with feces. The parasite can live for up to 5 years in humans, eventually burrowing into the mucosa of the duodenum as adults. Eggs produced by the adult female pass in the feces. Eosinophilia points to a parasite infection. The adult worm migrates to the small bowel and can cause duodenitis, leading to epigastric pain that is aggravated by food ingestion. Patients complain of diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and anorexia. Pulmonary manifestations can include wheezing, dyspnea, and hemoptysis. Patients may complain of a dry cough, and chronic infection may result in recurrent pulmonary symptoms that are suggestive of bacterial pneumonia. Diagnosis is usually made by detection of characteristic larvae in stool or by serology. Incorrect Options: Option A: Coccidiosis is associated with chronic tropical diarrhea. Option B: Giardia is associated with a malabsorption syndrome. Option C: Isospora belli is a parasite that causes chronic tropical diarrhea. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.stem: A patient is referred for evaluation of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. On upper endoscopy, he has scalloped mucosal folds in part of his small bowel with a relative paucity of folds in the area. Biopsy reveals villous atrophy with many lymphocytes and plasma cells infiltrating the lamina propria. Which of the following statements is true?
questions.stemHtml: A patient is referred for evaluation of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. On upper endoscopy, he has scalloped mucosal folds in part of his small bowel with a relative paucity of folds in the area. Biopsy reveals villous atrophy with many lymphocytes and plasma cells infiltrating the lamina propria. Which of the following statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The most frequently affected site is the proximal jejunum

options.label: B
options.text: It generally responds well to chemotherapy

options.label: C
options.text: It is the most common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) in adults

options.label: D
options.text: It is highly associated with inflammatory bowel disease

questions.answerText: The most frequently affected site is the proximal jejunum
questions.solution: Ans- A. The most frequently affected site is the proximal jejunum This patient’s endoscopic findings are consistent with refractory celiac disease, and the pathology is consistent with enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma (EATL). EATLs do not typically respond well to chemotherapy, but the main regimens tried are CHOP and alemtuzumab with CHOP. Of the patients who do respond to chemotherapy, 80% relapse within 5 years, and 85% die within 5 years of diagnosis. Surgery remains the primary treatment approach for patients with EATL. Those with local disease have a 60% 5-year survival rate, while those with advanced disease have a 25% 5-year survival rate. In the end, only about 20% are alive 5 years from the time of diagnosis. Finally, while EATLs can involve any part of the small bowel, it most frequently affects the proximal jejunum. Incorrect Answers: B. EATLs do not typically respond well to chemotherapy. C. An EATL is a type of peripheral T cell lymphoma (PTCL). PTCLs are aggressive neoplasms that constitute less than 15 percent of all non-Hodgkin lymphomas (NHLs) in adults. D. EATL is highly associated with celiac disease (gluten-sensitive enteropathy), and commonly diagnosed in adults from geographic areas with a high incidence of celiac disease (such as western part of Ireland and Northern Europe). Association with inflammatory bowel disease is not common. @Neet_pg_bot
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans- A. The most frequently affected site is the proximal jejunum

 

This patient’s endoscopic findings are consistent with refractory celiac disease, and the pathology is consistent with enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma (EATL). EATLs do not typically respond well to chemotherapy, but the main regimens tried are CHOP and alemtuzumab with CHOP. Of the patients who do respond to chemotherapy, 80% relapse within 5 years, and 85% die within 5 years of diagnosis. Surgery remains the primary treatment approach for patients with EATL. Those with local disease have a 60% 5-year survival rate, while those with advanced disease have a 25% 5-year survival rate. In the end, only about 20% are alive 5 years from the time of diagnosis. Finally, while EATLs can involve any part of the small bowel, it most frequently affects the proximal jejunum.

Incorrect Answers:

B. EATLs do not typically respond well to chemotherapy.

C. An EATL is a type of peripheral T cell lymphoma (PTCL). PTCLs are aggressive neoplasms that constitute less than 15 percent of all non-Hodgkin lymphomas (NHLs) in adults.

D. EATL is highly associated with celiac disease (gluten-sensitive enteropathy), and commonly diagnosed in adults from geographic areas with a high incidence of celiac disease (such as western part of Ireland and Northern Europe). Association with inflammatory bowel disease is not common.

questions.stemHtml: A 30-year-old female with a history of dysmenorrhea and pelvic pain presents with dyschezia, diarrhea, and bloating. You suspect rectovaginal endometriosis as the cause of her symptoms, which are more pronounced during menses. Which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Rectal endoscopic ultrasound is the first-line study for evaluation of rectovaginal endometriosis.

options.label: B
options.text: A double-contrast barium enema is the initial recommended imaging test for suspected endometriosis.

options.label: C
options.text: Sigmoidoscopy and colonoscopy are the most useful studies for the identification of bowel endometriosis.

options.label: D
options.text: Definitive therapy is hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and removal of extrapelvic lesions that are symptomatic.

questions.answerText: Definitive therapy is hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and removal of extrapelvic lesions that are symptomatic.
questions.solution: Correct Option D: Definitive therapy is hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and removal of extrapelvic lesions that are symptomatic. A trial of medical therapy is usually the initial line of treatment in patients with endometriosis, but surgical treatment is definitive. Since rectovaginal and bowel endometriosis coexist with other diseases, definitive treatment is hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with removal of rectovaginal lesions. Incorrect Options: Option A: Transvaginal ultrasound is the first study used for evaluation of rectovaginal endometriosis because rectal endoscopic ultrasound is associated with more discomfort and the need for sedation. After identification of rectovaginal endometriosis, rectal endoscopic ultrasound can be used to determine the distance from anal junction and the depth of infiltration when evaluating the need for surgery. Option B: Double-contrast barium enema may reveal information about partial bowel obstruction, but the information is not specific to endometriosis, so it is not useful for evaluation or initial diagnosis. Option C: Sigmoidoscopy and colonoscopy have limited utility since endometrial lesions do not usually penetrate the mucosa. @Neet_pg_bot

Incorrect Options:

Option A: Transvaginal ultrasound is the first study used for evaluation of rectovaginal endometriosis because rectal endoscopic ultrasound is associated with more discomfort and the need for sedation. After identification of rectovaginal endometriosis, rectal endoscopic ultrasound can be used to determine the distance from anal junction and the depth of infiltration when evaluating the need for surgery.

Option B: Double-contrast barium enema may reveal information about partial bowel obstruction, but the information is not specific to endometriosis, so it is not useful for evaluation or initial diagnosis.

Option C: Sigmoidoscopy and colonoscopy have limited utility since endometrial lesions do not usually penetrate the mucosa.

questions.stem: A 75-year-old male patient presents for evaluation of hematochezia. He has a history of atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, and diabetes and has been on warfarin for 2 years. He has been resuscitated with IV crystalloids and 3 units of packed red blood cells in the ED, and colonoscopy reveals several right-sided diverticula, including one that is actively bleeding. Which of the following is most appropriate for the management of this patient?
questions.stemHtml: A 75-year-old male patient presents for evaluation of hematochezia. He has a history of atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, and diabetes and has been on warfarin for 2 years. He has been resuscitated with IV crystalloids and 3 units of packed red blood cells in the ED, and colonoscopy reveals several right-sided diverticula, including one that is actively bleeding. Which of the following is most appropriate for the management of this patient?

options.label: C
options.text: Epinephrine injection to the bleeding diverticulum with hemostatic clipping as needed for stigmata

questions.answerText: Epinephrine injection to the bleeding diverticulum with hemostatic clipping as needed for stigmata
questions.solution: Correct Option C: Epinephrine injection to the bleeding diverticulum with hemostatic clipping as needed for stigmata Diverticular bleeding originates about 50% of the time from the right half of the colon, either at or proximal to the splenic flexure. One study demonstrated that the treatment of diverticular bleeding with epinephrine injection and either hemoclipping or multipolar probe coagulation did not result in any initial treatment failures and resulted in a 12% 30-day rebleeding rate. This study included patients who resumed anticoagulation for comorbidities. Six percent of patients required embolization by interventional radiology or surgery, and one patient had a post-coagulation syndrome. In the same study, the rate of continued bleeding in patients treated medically was 50%, and 35% of patients treated medically required surgery or embolization. Incorrect Options: Option A - Clip placement and angiography: Angiography is indicated in patients with severe bleeding in whom endoscopy has not revealed the bleeding site or when endoscopic hemostasis is not successful. It is also potentially useful in patients in whom severe rebleeding occurs. Actively bleeding diverticula can be identified endoscopically. Option B - Clip placement and emergency surgery : Emergency surgery is not indicated. Endoscopic management is appropriate. Option D - Coaptive coagulation inside the diverticulum : When thermal coagulation is utilized, it is in combination with epinephrine injection @Neet_pg_bot

In the same study, the rate of continued bleeding in patients treated medically was 50%, and 35% of patients treated medically required surgery or embolization.

Incorrect Options:

Option A - Clip placement and angiography: Angiography is indicated in patients with severe bleeding in whom endoscopy has not revealed the bleeding site or when endoscopic hemostasis is not successful. questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding modified barium swallow is correct?
questions.stemHtml: Which of the following statements regarding modified barium swallow is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Peristalsis is best evaluated in the upright position

options.label: B
options.text: Images are obtained in the anterior projection to best evaluate oropharyngeal function

options.label: C
options.text: Primary peristaltic waves manifests as an inverted “V”

options.label: D
options.text: Smooth tapering at the esophagogastric junction suggests normal relaxation

questions.answerText: Primary peristaltic waves manifests as an inverted “V”
questions.solution: Correct Option C: Primary peristaltic waves manifests as an inverted “V” The primary peristaltic wave manifests as an inverted “V” representing the tail of the bolus. Abnormalities of peristalsis are inferred by a retrograde escape of the bolus through the wavefront ultimately resulting in incomplete esophageal emptying. Incorrect Options: Option A - Peristalsis is best evaluated in the upright position: Peristalsis is best evaluated in the prone position so that clearance is not aided by gravity. Option B - Images are obtained in the anterior projection to best evaluate oropharyngeal function: The lateral projection is better for evaluation of the esophagus because it will capture the oropharynx, palate, proximal esophagus, and the proximal airway. Option D - Smooth tapering at the esophagogastric junction suggests normal relaxation : Normally the OGJ will become widely patent when approached by the bolus and impaired relaxation is suggested when there is either a smooth tapering at the EGJ or an impairment of bolus transit. Spastic contractions are demonstrated by a classic corkscrew appearing esophagus and are not normal. @Neet_pg_bot

Correct Option C: Primary peristaltic waves manifests as an inverted “V”

Incorrect Options:

Option A - Peristalsis is best evaluated in the upright position: Peristalsis is best evaluated in the prone position so that clearance is not aided by gravity.

Option B - Images are obtained in the anterior projection to best evaluate oropharyngeal function: The lateral projection is better for evaluation of the esophagus because it will capture the oropharynx, palate, proximal esophagus, and the proximal airway.

Option D - Smooth tapering at the esophagogastric junction suggests normal relaxation: Normally the OGJ will become widely patent when approached by the bolus and impaired relaxation is suggested when there is either a smooth tapering at the EGJ or an impairment of bolus transit.
